entries.what: The ladder's fights (deep16/data/fights.js, 09-27): the 8-bit game's set pieces rebuilt on the grid -- 28 of them, from the Hex floor (L1) to the sect blades (L9) -- each on a map the Code tab drew from the 8-bit game's scene text (data/maps.js), each foe from content/monsters.json with SRD sizes, speeds and reaches, and each fight sized hard for the four by the DMG table where the 8-bit game sized it for its guests (the entry card says what the 8-bit list was). Levels are by that table, not by where the 8-bit game fights them (the night crew at 4, holding the stair at 2).
entries.why: Griz, 09-27: 'get as many fights ready for testing as you can. We should start with boss fights from the 8-bit that don't involve water ... The otyugh fight should probably slot in there'; the approved rung plan; 'better to disconnect and then pull the fights from the simulator and slot into the 8-bit later'.

entries.what: Water on the grid, hand-waved: a creature that lives in the water keeps to it (bound: the otyugh, the Keeper, the naga -- they move there unslowed and reach out of it) or swims in it and comes ashore (the chuul); nobody else swims, and water is difficult ground for them. The Keeper fight starts the four at the water's foot (the 8-bit game's WADE IN), and it starts unseen.
entries.why: Griz, 09-27: 'we're going to have to figure out the water thing (we'll probably hand wave the chuul fight rather than add swimming (for example))'.

entries.what: The lake fight on the ladder: Barley wears the Ring of Binding (+3 CON saves; on rounds 1, 4, 7 and 10 the chuul must turn on him), as the 8-bit game's ring reads.
entries.why: content/text.json winters.ring (RULED 09-23); the ladder has no equip screen, so the lead wears it.

entries.what: The wagon yard on the ladder: Amara and Willem fight only to get to the horses -- each turn a step (15 ft) toward the stable gate and their spells; either one through the gate loses the fight (THEY GOT AWAY WITH THE HORSES), where the 8-bit game starts its chase.
entries.why: events.js S.wagonFight ('the pair fight only to get to the horses'); the ladder has no chase to hand off to.

entries.what: Level-1 sheets for the four (deep16/js/save.js SV.levelOne): drawn back from the 8-bit game's level-2 starts -- one max hit die plus CON (the starts are exactly two: Barley 13, Aurdin 6, Vivian 9, Lymen 12), the level-1 slot table (Aurdin two first-level slots; Lymen none, so no Smite), no Action Surge, Lay on Hands 5.
entries.why: Griz, 09-27: 'might as well add level 1, we'll want it eventually'; RULED 09-25: a max hit die at every level.

entries.what: The ladder's creatures wear CC0 stand-ins (tools/deep16-figures.json, all PROPOSED to his eye): Quaternius Alien (ettercap), GreenSpikyBlob (otyugh, and in stone grey the xorns), Monkroose (bugbear chief), Orc and Orc_Skull (hobgoblins), Tribal (gnolls), BlueDemon (stone giant; in brown the earth elementals), Dino (bulette), Cactoro (roper -- it wears a hat), Frog (chuul -- no crab in the packs), Ghost (cloaker), Glub (darkmantle), Squidle (grick), the snakes (naga, the Keeper), the slime (puddings, ochre jelly, gray ooze), Bat, Husky (hyenas), Wolf at two squares (worg); KayKit Adventurers graded for the people (guards, Hask's crew, duergar, the sect blades, the spell-weaver, Amara and Willem); the phase spider at three squares (the broodmother).
entries.why: Griz, 09-27: 'loose fits are better than no fits'; the Cowork seat's asset map (handoff-2026-09-27-deep16-drider-and-bestiary-assets.md sec. 3).

entries.what: Inside the 8-bit game DEEP16 fights the 8-bit scene's own foes (sized there for the guests), each on its DEEP16 fight's spot for that kind; one with no spot is set on the nearest free square beside a spot of its kind in turn (hidden or in the rock as that one is), else beside the fight's first foe, never in the party's lap; a party bigger than the map's entry takes the nearest free squares behind it.
entries.why: RULED 09-28 (Griz): the 8-bit's list is the roster; the placement is the seat's.

entries.what: The 8-bit game's dwarves on the grid (pyro_p0, halldor_p0, trooper_p0, brann_p0, hedda_p0, ingrith_p0, torvald_p0), LPC layers in the 8-bit LOOKS colours: the king in silver plate with a gold crown and a white winter beard; Halldor in iron plate; a trooper in mail and a nasal helm; Brann in steel plate with the war axe for his battleaxe; Hedda in mail; Ingrith in a white robe (her mail not drawn); the cleric hooded, a brown traveling cloak over a frock coat. Warhammers are drawn as the mace. Each squashed to a dwarf's build (tools/lpc-squash.py: short legs).
entries.why: Griz 09-28: guest art by LPC compose. LPC has no dwarf body and no warhammer.

entries.what: Torvald on the grid: 'He Will Not Be Held', at Deepholm's door (a new map: the made road's end, the step up to the door, the grille's bars either side, the bench). The card: 'A dwarf in a cleric's coat, a pack on his back and somewhere to be, and you fill the road. He will not be held.' He yields at half his hit points with his own words (deep.tvYield) on the card; killed outright, 'THE CLERIC IS DEAD ON THE MADE ROAD.' The 8-bit's AC 13, 40 HP and mace; WIS 16 and speed 25 drafted.
entries.why: Griz 09-28: 'under most circumstances it shouldn't end in a fight, but given the weight of the scene I think we should redo it in 16'. The door from deep.doorSee.

entries.what: The grid's opening cards inside the 8-bit game: 'CAUGHT OFF GUARD: they have the first round.' and 'THEY NEVER SAW YOU COMING: the first round is yours.' (the 8-bit battle's own two lines); the roper seen under the lamp, 'One of them is not a stalagmite, and the lamp has already shown you which.'; the lake without the ring, the 8-bit's own lake.risesNoRing; with it on someone other than Barley, the card names them.
entries.why: The 8-bit scene has already said who saw whom (its `surprised` / `revealed`), so DEEP16 rolls nothing and says so.

entries.what: Ottilie stops a party at the guano mine's mouth if anything it carries is always lit (an item's light with when: always; today only the Sunshaft Staff): '{name}. You can't go in there wielding that {item}. The light would spook the roost.' (or carrying it, seen glowing through the pack). LEAVE IT WITH HER / TURN BACK; left, it goes under her stool and back to the pack when the party is next at the mouth. The Sunshaft Staff's light drafted at the Light cantrip's 20 ft bright and 20 dim.
entries.why: Griz 09-28: the other light sources roost too; 'have the guy out front stop the players in the 8-bit if they have them equipped'; 'only things that are actively lit ... he can see the glow of the always on ones even when they are sheathed'; his line, the item named. The register gives the mouth's refusals to Ottilie (GalleriesModule/guano-galleries-DM.md §4). She keeps it because this game has no way to set a thing down (the staff is noSell).

entries.what: Shooting blind: an attack at a creature the attacker cannot see is at disadvantage, both games, as the SRD 5.1 has it; an unseen attacker has advantage, so two blind fighters roll straight.
entries.why: RULED 09-28: his first notion was a -4 ('shooting blind is just handled with a -4'); AMENDED the same day on his question -- the -4 was AD&D's number (2e: -4 to hit an unseen opponent), 'shouldn't be what the game does'. R.BLIND in js/rules.js keeps the -4 as a switch for both games.

entries.what: A torch takes a hand: a two-handed weapon takes both, a shield one, a torch one; a versatile weapon held with a torch hits for its one-handed die. Lighting one is an action (the SRD tinderbox); the Thief's Fast Hands make it a bonus. Dropped it burns where it fell; thrown (an action) it lands within 20 ft; doused it goes back in the pack; a lit one is spent.
entries.why: Griz 09-28: 'Aurdin would pretty much have to carry it lest lyman drop shield'. The action-or-bonus is a one-line switch (deep16/js/light.js LIGHT_COST), open for his word.

entries.what: Magic Missile may be aimed at a square the caster cannot see into (dark, magical darkness, fog): the darts fly and strike whatever hostile stands there; an empty square takes nothing but the slot. The card says AT THE DARKNESS.
entries.why: Griz 09-28: 'we have to do magic missile at the darkness gimmick somewhere in the game'. A switch (deep16/js/magic.js D.RULES.missilesAtTheDark), on by default; the set piece for it (the drow raid?) is his to place.

entries.what: Continual Flame asks for no ruby: a 2nd-level slot sets a heatless torch-bright flame on the weapon in hand, for good; it counts as always lit (Ottilie stops it at the roost's mouth).
entries.why: RULED 09-28: the rest spells are the game's only consumed components, 'nothing else consumes one'. Flagged: the SRD's 50 gp ruby is its balance.

entries.what: A torch lit in the field (ITEM, on a dark map) is carried by one hero with a free hand: the field's shadow opens wider and warmer round the party, a fight starts lit, and it burns till a rest or another map.
entries.why: The SRD torch burns an hour; the game has no clock between doors, so the map is the hour.

entries.what: The Mirror's eye, the pact of the Mirror's class feature (all its warlocks; Amara first): a mirror worn facing forward. In the cone before the wearer, a creature standing in any light cannot hide from her and gains nothing by being invisible. It shows nothing in the dark.
entries.why: RULED 09-28 (Griz, on the ear file's hold: 'I'll agree with Mirror Eye and it needing light. All Mirror Warlocks should get it as a class feature'). In place of the PHB's Awakened Mind (not SRD); the register's 'asking' stays a story note. The cone is the wearer's facing and a little past the two beside it (deep16/js/magic.js inMirror).

entries.what: The gimmick's home: in the cloaker's deep gallery, the first Magic Missile thrown at the darkness is a cutscene -- a close-up of the caster with the clip 'attacking the darkness', the cloaker hit, its face with 'AND THE DARKNESS ATTACKS BACK' -- and the cloaker comes for the caster.
entries.why: Griz 09-28: the mp3 is the livestreams' branding; his own storyboard ('a quick cutscene close-up of Aurdin and then that mp3, then a close up of the cloaker showing it hit, then big close up cloaker face'). The second line's clip is his to record (deep16/audio/the_darkness_attacks_back.mp3); the caption carries it till then.

entries.what: The SRD 5.1 is used as it stands (licensed, CC BY 4.0; an SRD spell may wear a new name). What the register names past the SRD (the Player's Handbook's) the game makes its own: our name, our words, a function of our own -- never the book's thing under a new label. The register keeps what words it likes for the table; this is about what the public game ships.
entries.why: RULED 09-28 (the ear file, dist-1, canon): his lean was 'sufficiently distinct' for a game a 12-year-old plays.

entries.what: Mirror's Gaze (Amara's 1st-level spell, in Hex's place), built on the SRD's Hunter's Mark: a bonus action, concentration; her hits on the marked one deal an extra 1d6 psychic, and while it is marked it cannot hide from her -- she always knows where it is, and being unseen gains it nothing against her. No curse on its checks.
entries.why: RULED 09-28 (dist-2, AMENDED: the name is his, 'Mirror's Gaze'). Hex is the PHB's, not the SRD's.

entries.what: Friends is dropped from Amara's cantrips; Minor Illusion (SRD, the warlock list) takes its place.
entries.why: RULED 09-28 (dist-3, canon): nothing in either game plays a Charisma contest where she'd cast it; Friends is the PHB's.

entries.what: Phantasmal Force is dropped from Willem's book; Blur (SRD, an illusion) takes its place. He keeps Mirror Image, Major Image, Hypnotic Pattern and his Ray of Frost.
entries.why: RULED 09-28 (dist-4, canon): Phantasmal Force is the PHB's.

entries.what: Amara's patron is the pact of the Mirror, a patron of our own in the Great Old One's place. Its expanded list, SRD spells, glass all through: 1st Silent Image, Hideous Laughter (and Glass Whisper, its own harm; and Command, the asking); 2nd Mirror Image, Detect Thoughts; 3rd Hypnotic Pattern, Clairvoyance; 4th Greater Invisibility, Confusion; 5th Mislead, Dominate Person. Its class feature is the Mirror's eye (#mirror-eye).
entries.why: RULED 09-28 (dist-5, canon). The register's patron is the Great Old One (RE-RULED 08-29: 'the Great Old One -- the Mirror'), the PHB's; the SRD has only the Fiend. Flagged: the SRD's patrons carry two spells a level, this one four at the 1st. TRIMMED 09-28g (Griz: 'Trim'): its 1st carries two, the SRD's patrons' count -- Glass Whisper and Command, the two his words named; Silent Image and Hideous Laughter (the seat's) are off it.

entries.what: Glass Whisper (the pact of the Mirror's own 1st-level harm, ours): one creature within 60 ft that can hear her, WIS save or 2d6 psychic (+1d6 a slot above the 1st), and on a failure it sees itself in the glass and cannot take reactions until the end of its next turn; half on a save and nothing more.
entries.why: RULED 09-28 (dist-6, his note 'Glass Whisper'): in the place of Dissonant Whispers, the PHB's Great Old One spell, not carried.

entries.what: The register's 'asking that arrives like the memory of an asking' is Command (SRD 5.1, 1st level): one word, WIS save, and the target obeys on its next turn (FLEE, GROVEL, HALT, DROP, APPROACH). It is on the pact of the Mirror's expanded list, as the SRD's own Fiend patron carries Command at the 1st; Amara knows it. Kat described it in her own words; the spell keeps its SRD name.
entries.why: RULED 09-28 (dist-7's open half; his words: 'if command is SRD we'll assume that's what Kat saw working and described in her own words, not change spell name' ... 'except it was a warlock not a cleric, so you're right unless warlocks have access to it'). The SRD Fiend's expanded spells are Burning Hands and Command at the 1st (dnd5eapi.co /subclasses/fiend), so a warlock's patron giving Command is the SRD's own shape. Flagged: it makes Amara's known spells seven at the 5th (the SRD's table says six). TRIMMED 09-28g (Griz: 'Trim'): Amara knows six at the 5th, the SRD's count -- Gaseous Form (OUT in the game) comes off her list for Command.

entries.what: An NPC of each SRD class, levels 1 to 6, built by the SRD's tables on the grid (DEEP16) to test every spell and feature before the story calls it in. Where an existing named NPC holds a class the generator builds that NPC by name (Higertha the half-orc druid; Torvald and Ingrith, clerics; Amara, warlock of the Mirror; Willem, wizard of illusion; and the others the register names); the rest are human, standard array (15, 14, 13, 12, 10, 8) by the class's priorities, named only by class and level ('Cleric 5'). HP the SRD's fixed average (the max-die rule is for the story-vital, by name). Subclass the SRD's one each (the warlock's the Mirror or the Fiend).
entries.why: RULED 09-28 (Griz: 'Higertha is half-orc Druid, see if other existing NPCs need classes built and human the rest of the classes'; 'except when matching existing NPCs, generic is good'). The handoff 09-28 npc-classes-to-six.

entries.what: Aurdin's book grows by Rope Trick (learned at wizard 3) and Tiny Hut (at 5) in the build's picks; the climb's level-up list offers both.
entries.why: RULED 09-28 ('The build's picks'). The resting spells are field spells only (#rope-trick, #tiny-hut).

entries.what: The Dome Whorl: a fist-sized whorl off the Dominion shore, clear as glass and cold; a wizard breaks one to raise Tiny Hut for the night. Percy sells it, 250 silver -- his shelf's first thing for sale (a part: he buys one back at his fifth).
entries.why: RULED 09-28: 'have the bead be a special snailshell we just invented - we'll put them as a dominion shore export', Percy's, not cheap. The name and the price are the seat's draft (the drafts stand, RULED 09-24). FOR THE COWORK SEAT: a Dominion-shore export to fold into the realm (the place is canon, THE TWO CANONS).

entries.what: Rope Trick in the 8-bit field: a short rest wherever a tent could go (outside, or down a dark working), the party up a rope into a hidden space; it takes a 2nd-level slot and a skein of Gulch Silk.
entries.why: RULED 09-28: 'the resting spells ... a short rest like the tent, spends a skein of Gulch Silk'. The SRD's needs a rope; the silk is the game's first consumed component.

entries.what: Tiny Hut in the 8-bit field: a long rest wherever a tent could go, the same rest the inn gives (the story clocks count it, the morning's spells, the save); cast from the book as the SRD's ritual (no slot, never prepared); it breaks a Dome Whorl.
entries.why: RULED 09-28 ('making sure their long-rests are counted with the others and allow saves'). The SRD's needs a small crystal bead; here the whorl.

entries.what: Lymen's paladin list grows by Command, Branding Smite and Magic Weapon, and his Oath of Devotion keeps Protection from Evil and Good and Sanctuary ready from the 3rd, in both games (one law: js/rules.js R.PALADIN_SPELLS, R.oathSpells). The 8-bit battle casts all five: Command, one of four words (GROVEL, HALT, FLEE, DROP), and the commanded foe's next turn is spent obeying (the dead and the witless don't understand it); Branding Smite's +2d6 radiant rides the next weapon hit and takes invisibility off the one struck; Magic Weapon makes an ally's plain weapon +1 (+2 from a 4th-level slot) and magical; Protection from Evil and Good gives the otherworldly (aberration, celestial, elemental, fey, fiend, undead) disadvantage on the warded one and keeps their fear off it; Sanctuary makes a foe save WIS to strike the warded one, else it turns on another, and it ends when the warded one attacks or casts at a foe. Each lasts the fight (ten rounds); the 8-bit battle keeps no concentration, as with Bless and Hold Person.
entries.why: RULED 09-28g (Griz, on 'Should the 8-bit's own battle get Lymen's new spells?'): 'yeah, they have to be able to transfer back and forth from 16bit fights'.

entries.what: In the 8-bit battle a bonus-action spell costs the bonus action, not the action, as on the grid (SRD 5.1): Divine Favor, Shield of Faith, Branding Smite, Magic Weapon, Sanctuary, Healing Word, Spiritual Weapon. The hero still has the action (FIGHT, an item, a cantrip); a levelled spell with it is greyed, the SRD's rule. Before this every 8-bit spell took the action.
entries.why: The seat's, 09-28g, from the same ruling: a spell that crosses should play the same on both sides, and Branding Smite taking the whole turn before its blow would have made it nothing in the 8-bit. Divine Favor and Shield of Faith get cheaper for Lymen: the playtest's to say.

entries.what: Ingrith is a cleric 4 in the 8-bit game too: the SRD's average HP by the d8 (31, where the fighter sheet had 36), slots 4/3, WIS; the drafted list (Sacred Flame, Guidance; Bless, Cure Wounds, Healing Word, Shield of Faith; Aid, Lesser Restoration) and the Life Domain's Spiritual Weapon; the Life Domain, the SRD's one (heavy armour, so her chain mail and shield stand at AC 18; Disciple of Life; Preserve Life). The 8-bit battle runs her turn as a cleric: a friend down gets Healing Word and the mace after; two or more low, Preserve Life; one low, Cure Wounds; two or more dead things, Turn Undead; the first round against more than one, Bless; else the floating weapon and the mace. The old heals counter is retired; a save made with the fighter sheet walks her on as the cleric, as hurt as she was. On the grid the overlay steps aside: her sheet is the cleric's.
entries.why: RULED 09-28g (Griz: 'Yes, she's meant to be Cleric.'). The domain is the seat's: the register names none (Cleric of Rekknar), the class-NPC rule gives the SRD's one, and it fits a guest who heals and keeps her armour.

entries.what: What the 8-bit pack and gear do on the grid, checked (dev/bench16.js mode=items): the pack crosses as it stands (no crossbow lent inside the 8-bit game), and the named items and the pie now do there what they do in the 8-bit battle: the Winnower knocks one flat on a critical; the Greyseam knife's Sneak Attack poisons (CON 13, till the end of its next turn); the Door-Shield's ward (a miss at its bearer on a natural 15 or more, 3%: +3 AC to the party till the bearer's turn); Marta's bat-wing pie eaten in the fight (+5 HP, +1 CON saves, the fight's alone: it crosses back without the +5, never read as Aid); the elixir cures paralysis too. Already there: potions, kits, antitoxin, oil, torches, the Flame Tongue, the Cloak of Displacement, the Ring of Protection, the Sunshaft staff's DC and its light, the Ring of Binding at the lake.
entries.why: Griz 09-28g: 'Also need to make sure items are being loaded into the 16bit fights.'

entries.what: The black pudding's and the gray ooze's acid eat weapons and armour for the fight only; nothing is worn down for good.
entries.why: RULED 09-28g (Griz, on 'Should the ooze's acid wear gear down for good?'): 'No'. (The SRD's corrosion is permanent.)

entries.what: The Path of the Sand, Talmok's barbarian path, our own in the Totem Warrior's place. 3rd: FIRST BLOOD -- when he takes damage and isn't raging, he can rage as his reaction (a use spent); DOWN IN THE SAND -- raging, once on each of his turns, a creature no bigger than Large that he hits in melee saves STR (8 + proficiency + STR) or goes prone. 6th: ANSWER BACK -- raging, when a creature in his reach misses him in melee, his reaction is one melee attack back. Built on the grid (deep16/js/features.js); on the Pocket DM as ?npc=talmok (barbarian 3, his register numbers and pit fists, no handaxes to throw). The ladder's card keeps his bestiary sheet, whose rage-on-hit and prone fists are the 3rd level's two features in stat-block form. Levels 7-9 (09-28h): no new path feature till the 10th; the barbarian's own -- FERAL INSTINCT at 7 (advantage on initiative; caught unaware, he acts on his first turn if he rages first), BRUTAL CRITICAL at 9 (one more weapon die on a melee critical: his pit fists have none, so it adds nothing to them), rage +3 at 9, and the ASIs past his register's 3rd (STR 18 at 4, 20 at 8). Built at any level as ?npc=talmok:7 and on the tester ladder (?ladder&party=ours); the story's Talmok stays 3. 09-28h: PIT FISTS (3rd) -- his unarmed strikes hit for 1d4 + STR, 1d6 from the 6th (js/rules.js damageExpr, both games); the 8-bit Talmok's Pit Fists 1d4+3 (content/monsters.json; a flat 4 before), the grid's bestiary sheet the same.
entries.why: RULED 09-28g (Griz, on the subclasses past the SRD: 'Sufficiently distinct'): the register's 'rages on first blood, wrestles to the sand' (npcs-by-location.md §TALMOK) made the path's own; the Bear's resistance to everything is the PHB's and is not carried. 09-28h (Griz: 'can we do the levels for the original classes up to nine' -- 'the off SRD ones we made to 9'; 'AI now, buttons later'). RULED 09-28h (Griz, asked why the fists had no die, so Brutal Critical added nothing: "Almost certainly, but I don't know why they didn't already"). They had none because the register's pit fists were built as the SRD 5.1 unarmed strike, a flat 1 + STR.

entries.what: The Rimeglass, Willem's arcane tradition, our own in the School of Illusion's place: illusion with the cold in it. 2nd: RIME DOUBLES -- a blow that breaks one of his false images (Mirror Image) breaks rime over the one who struck: its speed 10 ft less till the end of its next turn. 6th: RIME STEP -- when he casts an illusion of the 1st level or more, he steps 10 ft through the rime (a teleport, to the square farthest from his foes). Built on the grid; Willem (wizard 5) has the 2nd's in the wagon yard. Levels 7-9 (09-28h): no new tradition feature till the 10th. Past his register's 5th, the seat's picks, illusion with the cold in it: Sleet Storm, Fear, Slow (3rd); Phantasmal Killer, Greater Invisibility, Ice Storm (4th); Cone of Cold, Mislead, Hold Monster (5th); below it Color Spray, Magic Missile, Sleep, Hold Person; the cantrips Chill Touch and Shocking Grasp; INT 19 at 8; Mage Armor up when he is built away from his 5th. Built at any level as ?npc=willem:9 and on the tester ladder; the story's Willem stays 5.
entries.why: RULED 09-28g (Griz: 'Sufficiently distinct'); his cold is his own word ('Willem is a frosty person', 09-28), the doubles his register's Mirror Image, the step his office of covering the going. 09-28h (Griz: 'the off SRD ones we made to 9'): the list is the seat's draft, standing as approved; every spell on it casts on the grid.

entries.what: The Window, the cleric's domain of Tronupholen, the Fey in the Mirror (Kat's), our own in the Trickery Domain's place. Its spells, always prepared: 1st Disguise Self, Silent Image; 3rd Blur, Pass without Trace ('close the ground'); 5th Hypnotic Pattern, Clairvoyance. 1st: THE HAND ON THE NECK (WIS a long rest) -- a bonus action, a touch: the first blow that would land on the touched before the mender's next turn is rolled again, and the second roll stands (the glass takes it). 2nd: THE DOUBLING (Channel Divinity) -- two glass doubles step out of her mirror, and a blow at her may strike one instead (Mirror Image's odds). 6th: THE SHOWING (Channel Divinity) -- one creature within 30 ft that can see her mirror saves WIS or is shown something in the glass and can do nothing till the end of its next turn. On the Pocket DM as ?npc=katarina (human, at any level: her level is unruled in the register), leather and a shield, a mace. Its spells at the 7th: Greater Invisibility, Confusion; at the 9th: Mislead, Hold Monster (all four cast on the grid). 8th: DIVINE STRIKE -- once on each of her turns, a creature she hits with a weapon attack takes 1d8 psychic more (the glass shows it a crack). On the tester ladder (?ladder&party=ours) at every level 1-9. 09-28h: Katarina's register level is 3 (deep16/js/classes.js NPC.NAMED.katarina lvl 3).
entries.why: RULED 09-28g (Griz: 'Kat supposed to be Cleric of trickster deity trapped in mirror'). The names are the register's field words (serial-castegut/BIBLE.md 08-27: 'the hand on the neck', 'close the ground', 'the doubling'; 'three of her'); the functions are new, not the PHB's Blessing of the Trickster, Invoke Duplicity or Cloak of Shadows. Tronupholen shows, never speaks (08-13i). 09-28h (Griz: 'the off SRD ones we made to 9'): the seat's drafts; Divine Strike is the SRD Life Domain's 8th, in her god's own kind. RULED 09-28h (Griz): "at campaign start she's just hit 3".

entries.what: The Vigil, the cleric's domain of Dvalgarda, the Ward of the Dormant (Torvald's): the register names no domain, so it is our own. Its spells, always prepared: 1st Sanctuary, Protection from Evil and Good; 3rd Hold Person, Warding Bond; 5th Spirit Guardians, Glyph of Warding (not built: not cast). 1st: KEEPER'S WARD (WIS a long rest) -- a bonus action, one he can see within 30 ft (or himself): the next damage it takes before his next turn is cut by 1d8 + his cleric level. 2nd: HOLD THE DOOR (Channel Divinity) -- each foe within 10 ft saves STR or is shoved 10 ft away from him. 6th: WAKEFUL -- magic cannot put him, or one of his within 10 ft, to sleep. Built on the grid; Torvald (cleric 5) carries the 1st and 2nd at Deepholm's door. Its spells at the 7th: Guardian of Faith, Freedom of Movement; at the 9th: Hold Monster, Dispel Evil and Good (all four cast on the grid). 8th: DIVINE STRIKE -- once on each of his turns, a creature he hits with a weapon attack takes 1d8 radiant more (the Dormant's cold light). Past his register's 5th, the seat's picks: Protection from Energy, Mass Healing Word, Death Ward, Banishment, Mass Cure Wounds, Greater Restoration; WIS 18 at 8. Built at any level as ?npc=torvald:9 and on the tester ladder; the story's Torvald stays 5.
entries.why: RULED 09-28g (Griz, on 'Torvald has no domain': 'Sufficiently distinct'). Grounded in the register's Dvalgarda, Ward of the Dormant, whose sect keeps the vigil over the sleeping Silver and the egg (pantheon.md, CANON 08-28), and in his own fight's card: 'He will not be held.' 09-28h (Griz: 'the off SRD ones we made to 9'): the seat's drafts; Freedom of Movement for his card's 'He will not be held'.

entries.what: The tester ladder (?ladder&party=ours) builds our four as their grown builds at every level, their register's own included; one of ours who is that rung's foe (Willem in the Wagon Yard, Talmok on the Card's Top) is swapped for an alternate: Higertha, then a paladin (deep16/js/classes.js NPC.ours, NPC.ALTS).
entries.why: RULED 09-28h (Griz): "grown builds please"; "swap in alternates (your choice) rather than mirror" -- Higertha the seat's choice (a named NPC who stands at any level).

entries.what: A hooded lantern (50 sp at the Provisioner's and the Chandler's): bright 30 ft and dim 30 more; hood down, dim light 5 ft only and no bright light, so nothing light-shy is dazzled and a roost sleeps. It takes a hand like a torch, is never thrown, and is not spent: doused or put away it goes back in the pack. On the grid: ITEM lights it (under a roost, hood down), HOOD DOWN / HOOD UP, SET DOWN, DOUSE, TAKE UP; HOOD UP is refused under a roost. In the 8-bit fight the hood is implicit: under a roost the lantern lights the place dimly and nothing wakes; elsewhere it is a 30-ft torch. The camp's A LIGHT IN HAND walks in with either. Sleet does not put it out (its flame is not exposed).
entries.why: SRD 5.1 Hooded Lantern (5 gp; bright 30, dim 30; hooded: dim 5 ft) at the x10 economy (#economy). RULED 09-29 (Griz: 'like a mode that sort of lights and doesn't wake the bats'; 'I meant to cancel the no hood function decision'). Seat's calls: no oil to count (no fight runs six hours); the hood as the turn's free object interaction; sleet spares it.

entries.what: A generic druid NPC on the grid is a Circle of the Land druid of the Underdark: its circle spells (always prepared) are Web at 3, Stinking Cloud at 5, Greater Invisibility at 7 and Insect Plague at 9 (the SRD's list, the built ones; spider climb, gaseous form, stone shape and cloudkill left off). Higertha keeps the mountain (#higertha-druid): Spike Growth at 3, Lightning Bolt at 5, Stoneskin at 7.
entries.why: The SRD's Circle of the Land needs a land; the Pit is underground. The seat's call, 09-29 (Higertha to nine); a spec may name another land.

entries.what: WILD SHAPE offers the bestiary's beasts by the Circle of the Land's rule: the wolf, the wolf spider and the axe beak from 2 (CR 1/4, no flying or swimming), the giant frog from 4 (swimming allowed), the giant spider from 8 (CR 1); a Large shape stands in the druid's own square, and the beast's whole attack rides (the spiders' poison, the frog's grip). OWN SHAPE, a bonus action, ends it early.
entries.why: SRD 5.1 Wild Shape and the Land circle's CR table, limited to the sheets the grid has; the button and the pick RULED wanted 09-29 (Griz: 'druid beast form ... we'll have to do that').

entries.what: Enlarge gives no reach: the SRD 5.1 text grants +1d4 on weapon hits, advantage on STR checks and saves, and one size category, nothing about reach. The +5 ft the grid gave on 09-29 (a runner's build on Griz's 'might') is kept as a house-rule switch, off: D.RULES.enlargeReach (deep16/js/magic.js), read by G.reachOf.
entries.why: Griz 09-29: 'check rules if you can, that was my remember guess' -- checked, the SRD says no reach; the switch keeps the option.

entries.what: Calling Herbs (content/items.json callingherbs, 500 sp, sold only at Mama's Pharmakaiea): charcoal, incense and herbs Mama mixes; a wizard burns one bundle each time he casts Find Familiar, a new shape included.
entries.why: RULED 09-29, Griz: 'i'd like to add a material component for 500 sp only mama sells despite our normal hand-wave of components' (the SRD's 10 gp of charcoal, incense and herbs, priced up and placed with Mama, who mixes).

entries.what: Find Familiar's shape is picked from what lives on the ground under the party (js/rules.js R.FAM_GROUND / R.famForms): on the world map by tile (snow: snowy owl; fields: owl, rat; forest: owl, spider; water: frog, poisonous snake; stone and gulch: bat, spider, snake; cave mouths: bat, rat, spider), off it the caves' (bat, rat, spider) or the town's (rat, owl). Forms with no DEEP16 sheet yet (hawk, raven, cat, weasel, lizard, crab, octopus, fish, sea horse) are left off the pick. The snowy owl is the owl's regional form (the same numbers).
entries.why: Griz 09-29: 'we can do it from the menu on the worldmap menu and select by biome'; the lists are the seat's draft; the snowy owl came with the generated sheets ('SNOWY REGIONAL FORM').

entries.what: In an 8-bit fight the familiar rides the wizard's shoulder: if he makes no attack roll on his turn, the first ally to attack after it has advantage; if he does, his own first attack roll that turn has it. The foes never pick it; a blast that catches the wizard catches it whatever his save (at 0 it is gone, flags.familiarGone; the ritual calls it back). 09-30: the help is drawn -- it goes from his shoulder (or heel) to the target just before the roll it helps (his own first attack, a spell's first ray, the spiritual weapon's swing, or the first ally's blow) and back: the fliers arc (14 frames out, 10 there, 14 home), the others run the ground line. The bat loops about his head (a figure-eight in front of him); in the 8-bit the bat still helps ("8bit should be fine as is").
entries.why: RULED 09-29, Griz: 'my notion at giving 8-bit the help action of the familiar without adding a choice to the combat. First ally to attack after wizards turn if the wizard doesn't attack should work'; and 'not targeted by AI but subject to splash damage that includes the wizard, even if wizard saves'. 09-30, Griz: "I thought it would fly to help after aurdin picked a spell to attack with but before the spell went off, and fly from aurdin to target before allies attack lands when aurdin doesn't target on his turn"; the bat: "correct" (about his head in the 8-bit too). Geometry and timing a runner's draft (js/familiar.js).

entries.what: On the grid the familiar has no initiative: its turn comes right after its caster's. A touch spell on one not beside him goes by the familiar when a square beside that one is within the familiar's movement (flier or walker, from his square while it rides); it goes as the spell is cast and its own turn is the rest of that movement, spent heading home; not when he has ordered it to Help that turn, and an owl that carried one does not help that round. The owls help on their own (Flyby), the bat never, the others on his order (FAMILIAR: HELP on his SKILLS, free: SRD 'it always obeys your commands'; FAMILIAR: STAY calls it off); a caster the fight runs orders it himself. It rides again once it gets back into his square (5 ft to spare from beside him); short of it when its movement runs out, it holds a square and the foes may strike it. Out on the field the bat stand-in is drawn up in the air; riding, it loops about his head. AMENDED 09-30: the bat helps on his order like the others (it keeps its place about his head); in the 8-bit it helps as ever.
entries.why: RULED 09-30, Griz: "I'd put the familiars 'turn' after his casters ... if my familiar is out and I cast a touch spell on someone not next to me - it should fail if it's out of the familiars movement ... (only way a familiar is on a square is if it runs out of movement - at which time it would enter enemy targeting"; the bat "flutter around his head". The seat's calls: the ordered one picks the foe the party is on (as the owl does); the AI's casters order it; +5 ft to step into his square. Built deep16/js/familiar.js (09-30). Griz 09-30: "i think the bat not helping is out of balance and should be orderable in the 16 and let it keep doing it in the 8".

entries.what: What each familiar lends its caster while it is in the fight (js/rules.js R.FAMILIARS perk): rat darkvision 30 ft; bat sonar 15 ft (blindsight: any dark, the unseen); poisonous snake senses the hidden and the invisible within 15 ft (as sight), +1 to the save DC of his charm spells (R.CHARM_SPELLS), advantage on his Persuasion (a familiar's Help on a check, SRD); spider Web Walker and +1 to his Web's DC; frog: he is never caught off guard (a croak, js/audio.js croak). A perk is its caster's, whoever that is (the NPC casters and the Pocket DM's too). And on a dark map with no light, on a hero's turn, the grid is drawn through that hero's own senses: what he does not sense darker, darkvision grey, blindsight cool with a ping (deep16/js/light.js senseMap). In the 8-bit (no ranges): the rat's and the bat's caster sees in any dark; the snake's sees the invisible and the `unseen` foes (the keeper, the cube, the roper) plainly; a charm spell +1 (no hero spell charms yet); Persuasion with advantage, and when the party's best hand rolls he ranks +3 for the pick; the spider's caster is not held by a foe's web spit, and his Web +1; the frog's caster acts in a surprised first round (no assassin's crit on him) and the croak sounds.
entries.why: RULED 09-30, Griz: "rat grants nightvision, spider buffs web spell and gives 'webwalk' ... snake sense hidden within 15 feet (counts as vision)" · "Agreed with vision range." · "EXCELLENT call on the frog. will need audible." · "Snake still charm related spells, diplomacy and persuasion checks by caster" · "when map = no light source and player turn, active player vision filter on dark map (i.e. bat familiar sonar sight filter unless light on map)". The ranges were the seat's proposal, agreed; the +1s, the advantage, the croak's sound and the filter's look are the seat's drafts. The 8-bit reading of the 09-30 perks: a runner's draft (js/familiar.js, js/battle.js, js/deep.js EV.check; bench8 perks/perks2).

entries.what: The summons on the grid (deep16/data/summons.js D.SUMMON / D.summonPool, deep16/js/grimoire.js summonSpell): a summoning spell's pool is the bestiary itself, read by creature type and CR (a creature joins by being drawn into data/foes.js; `summon: false` keeps a story's own out; named, bound and class-built sheets and familiars never answer). The caster picks the creature, and the count is the most the SRD's options allow of it (x2 at a 5th-level slot for Conjure Animals); the AI's casters take the most worth (its best blow times its blows times the count, its HP as a wall). They appear on the free squares he can see nearest the point within 60 ft, take one initiative for the lot, fight under the AI (ai.js brute), vanish at 0 HP and all together when his concentration ends; they keep no fight going and cross nothing back to the 8-bit game. Conjure Woodland Beings is built on the same frame and waits, greyed, for the first fey. The ranger's 3rd is Conjure Animals too (SRD).
entries.why: RULED 09-30, Griz: "1 - I like it. Build a frame so that it's pulling those selections from a place where more to choose from might go as the world expands?" (the seat's proposal: the caster picks from the beasts we have by count and CR; they fight under the AI as if commanded, not the SRD's defend-only). The worth formula, the placement and the ranger's list are the seat's.

entries.what: The walls on the grid (deep16/js/walls.js; B.walls read by grid.js through G.wallAt): each is the SRD 5.1's line form, a straight run of squares laid across the caster's line to the point he picks, centred on it (one click; the ring and the dome forms are not built). Wall of Fire 60 ft, opaque, lit along its length; its burning side is the one away from him. Wall of Thorns 60 ft, blocks sight, 20 ft more a square. Wall of Stone 60 ft (the SRD allows ten 10-ft panels), bars the way and the eye; whoever stands where it rises is pushed out, his own to his side, the rest to the far one; the panels' AC and hit points are not built -- it stands till his concentration goes. Wind Wall 50 ft: arrows, bolts and thrown weapons across it miss; a small flier cannot cross; sight passes; the gases it keeps back are not built. The AI raises the burning ones (fire, thorns) where they catch the most of the other side; the stone and the wind are the player's. The wizard's and the sorcerer's class lists carry Wall of Fire and Wall of Stone; Higertha's mountain gets Wall of Stone at 9.
entries.why: The druid to twelve (Griz 09-29: "please complete druid to 12"), the handoff's step 2 (WALLS). The line form, the lengths, the burning side, the push, the AI's reach and the looks are the seat's; the damage, saves and costs are the SRD's.

entries.what: Polymorph, Dominate Beast, Charm Person and Animal Friendship on the grid (deep16/js/grimoire.js, deep16/js/features.js F.morph, ai.js heroes). Polymorph: the new shape is one of the world's beasts (deep16/data/summons.js D.pool, the summons' place) of the target's CR or level or less; the player picks, the AI makes a foe the weakest it can and never polymorphs a friend; the target keeps its footprint. Dominate Beast: the beast fights for the caster's side under the AI while concentration holds and saves again each time it is hurt; it keeps no fight going for them and is still the 8-bit's foe when the fight ends. A charm (Charm Person, Animal Friendship) takes its charmer off the charmed one's list of targets; harm to it on a turn of the charmer's side breaks it (the source of a blow read as whoever's turn it is). The charms were added last to each class's list (druid, bard, ranger, wizard, sorcerer), so what the NPCs prepare mostly stands.
entries.why: The druid to twelve (Griz 09-29: "please complete druid to 12"), the handoff's steps 3 and 4 (SHAPES, CHARM / DOMINATE). The mechanics are the SRD 5.1's; the picks, the AI's use and the harm-by-turn reading are the seat's.

entries.what: Antilife Shell, Plant Growth, Cloudkill and Giant Insect on the grid. Antilife Shell (deep16/js/walls.js): no creature but the undead and constructs steps across its 10-ft edge (grid.js stepCost via G.shellBars) or lands a melee blow across it (battle.js: the blow is turned; the AI may yet waste a swing on it); the caster moving so that the set of creatures inside changes ends it. Plant Growth: the road maps' grass squares within 100 ft of the point, 20 ft more a square, for the fight; no exclusions; greyed where nothing grows. Cloudkill (deep16/js/grimoire.js): obscuring fog (B.darks kind 'kill'), CON 5d8 on entering it the first time on a turn or starting a turn in it, rolling two squares straight away from its caster at the start of his turn; a Gust of Wind or a Wind Wall scatters it; the Underdark druid's circle spell at 9, the wizard's and the sorcerer's 5th. Giant Insect: the summons frame's fixed kinds (three giant spiders; the centipedes, wasps and scorpion when drawn), dealt in right after him on his roll. Tree Stride and the one-minute conjures wait.
entries.why: The druid to twelve (Griz 09-29: "please complete druid to 12"), the handoff's step 6. The mechanics are the SRD 5.1's; the grass as the plants, the drift's straight line, the shell's turned blow and the insects' place in the order are the seat's.

entries.what: The camp's CAST AHEAD shows only what someone in the party has on their list (known, or preparable today); with nothing to cast, the row itself is gone. Conjure Elemental joins it (a minute to cast: the camp's, never the fight's): whoever has it prepared and a 5th-level slot spends the slot; the elemental (the world's of CR 5 or less, the earth elemental first; the xorn is one too) walks in beside him on his side, with its own initiative, run by the fight, and holds his concentration -- the class AI values that concentration above any other spell; if it breaks the elemental breaks loose, hostile to its caster's side, a foe like any other (it keeps the fight going, and is not the 8-bit game's to count). Tree Stride is left out; Conjure Minor Elementals and Conjure Fey wait.
entries.why: RULED 09-30, Griz: "We'll need to revisit the campfire precast interface since we're adding potentials - what's in there should be dependent on party members. Let's add the earth elemental to camp and hold off on the rest." · "tree stride ... leave it out for now". The loose elemental is the SRD's ("it becomes hostile toward you and your companions"); the side it takes, the xorn in the list and the AI's hold on the concentration are the seat's.

entries.what: The class feature gaps on the grid (deep16/js/features.js, rules.js, grimoire.js, magic.js, tactics.js, classes.js; bench mode `features`): the monk's Patient Defense, Step of the Wind and Evasion (7; RU.evasion, the rogue's too -- and not while incapacitated); the Devotion paladin's Turn the Unholy (fiends and undead, a WIS save, turned for ten of its own turns or till hurt; class NPCs only -- Lymen keeps Sacred Weapon); the bard's Countercharm (advantage on saves against frightened or charmed within 30 ft; hearing and silence are not modelled); the sorcerer's Twinned (the generic sorcerer's second option; not for concentration spells or Chain Lightning; cost the spell's level, 1 for a cantrip), Careful (up to CHA-mod friends spared, in the order they save) and Heightened (the player picks the foe); the warlock's Pact of the Tome for the generic Fiend warlock (Fire Bolt, Sacred Flame, Vicious Mockery) and of the Blade for a spec (a rapier by default) -- the Chain waits for its sheets, Amara has none; Dark One's Own Luck (taken without asking when a save with something at stake falls short by 10 or less, or the web's break-free check); Mindless Rage (a charm or a fright suspended while he rages, back after if its caster still holds it); the Hunter's Escape the Horde (the generic Hunter's), Multiattack Defense and Steel Will (a spec's); the Thief's Supreme Sneak. Found and fixed: the turned (Turn Undead's) were set free by the end-of-turn sweep of their caster's fright, so an AI cleric's Turn Undead did nothing.
entries.why: The class NPCs' feature gaps (handoff-2026-09-30-druid-to-twelve.md §6), Griz 09-30: "Class feature gap proceed". Built by a Sonnet runner; the SRD 5.1's rules; the named choices are the runner's and the seat's, his to overrule.

entries.what: HIDDEN MECHANIC (never shown to a player): Lisbet Crane's Charm (content/items.json `charm`, a ring, 5 sp, Charms & Chalk in Silverton) makes whoever wears it immune to being frightened, in both games -- the 8-bit's Moan never takes the wearer (and says nothing: a resisted Moan prints no line); on the grid a failed save against a fright simply holds (RU.save: the card shows the real roll and the outcome, never why). Its words stay "Lisbet's charm. No promises made." The rule lives in js/rules.js R.fearWard.
entries.why: RULED 09-30, Griz: "that lady who sells an equipable charm in silverton - let's make that charm grant immune to fear in the mechanics, but not say so anywhere the player sees".

entries.what: CHANNEL DIVINITY is a list of its own on the grid's ring, beside SPELLS, with the uses left in its name: Sacred Weapon and Turn the Unholy (the Devotion paladin, Lymen too), Preserve Life and Turn Undead (the Life cleric; Preserve Life's button new: the lowest first, none past half), our domains' Doubling, Showing, Hold the Door. In the 8-bit, Lymen's SKILL shows CHANNEL DIVINITY (1/1), which opens Sacred Weapon and Turn the Unholy (the fiends and undead before him save WIS or cower, as the cleric's Turn Undead makes them).
entries.why: RULED 09-30, Griz: "should the channel divinity be a button similar to spells?" -- "3 yes"; Lymen's Turn the Unholy: "pretty sure he's supposed to have it".

entries.what: A charm holds a hero the player runs as it holds the AI's: a charmed one cannot attack its charmer, aim a harmful spell at it, or take an opportunity attack at it (battle.js canHit and the attack, magic.js targetWhy, moveAlong); the refusal says so and spends nothing. And Fear, Phantasmal Killer and Weird bite on the grid: the fright a spell lays holds as long as the spell (the end-of-turn sweep of a caster's frights spares a spell's), so the feared flee -- Heroism is the answer (Lymen's from 4), and Lisbet's charm, hidden.
entries.why: RULED 09-30, Griz: "1 yes 2 yes" (on "fix Fear so it bites?" -- his lean before: "biting can be good" -- and "enforce charm on heroes you run?").

entries.what: Pyro at 12 (content/heroes.json, deep16/js/classes.js NPC.NAMED.pyro): the Champion; STR 20 by the fighter's 12th-level ASI (his register's 18 at 9); HP 112 (the 9's average on); his off-hand the SRD Mace of Disruption (content/items.json macedisruption, 'clearly magical': magic, its 20/20 light while drawn); Dwarven Plate +3 (kingsplate: the SRD's Dwarven Plate is +2, ours +3 by his word; its shove-reduction reaction not built); the King's Mantle (kingsmantle: +5 to saving throws against spells -- name and words the seat's). The 8-bit guest is 12 too now (the measure holds him back), and the road weighs him as one guest, not two (js/deep.js GUEST_WEIGHT).
entries.why: RULED 09-30, Griz: 'Gonna have to Pyro NPC up to 12, he's key', 'his off-hand to be a mace of disruption if it's in our available magic items via SRD, clearly magical'; 09-30b: 'Also give him +3 dwarven plate, and a cloak +5 to saves vs spells.' The ASI, the name and the weight are the seat's.

entries.what: Hammer and Tongs, our fighting style (the Champion's Additional Fighting Style at 10, Pyro's): fighting with a one-handed weapon in each hand, light or not, one of the Attack action's swings may be the off-hand's -- besides Two-Weapon Fighting's bonus-action strike. At 12 that is five swings a turn: three by Extra Attack (5 and 11), one off-hand in the action, one off-hand as the bonus action (deep16/js/pyro.js, js/pyro.js).
entries.why: RULED 09-30, Griz: 'unless there's a fighting style (make it up if it's not) that gives him an extra attack with off-hand'; 09-30b: 'Yes regarding offhand' (the seat's reading, five swings at 12). Name and words the seat's.

entries.what: Pyro's measure (deep16/js/pyro.js, js/pyro.js): every fight he walks in, both games. Phase 1: one swing of the plain mace and his turn is over; the white mace at his belt. Phase 2 (he is at half HP, or one of the party is down): he draws the Mace of Disruption, two swings a turn, says his piece, and each of the party's XP is halved (the level kept). Phase 3 (one of the party leaves the fight -- on the grid, out the way they came in; in the 8-bit, the party's RUN): the white mace into his main hand, full level 12 to the end, then the save is loaded (FOUND WANTING). Down: the fight ends there and the save is loaded (THE KING FALLS). On the grid's own ladders and as a foe he fights at full from the first round. His lines (pyro.m2Down, m2Hurt, m3; fail.pyro, fail.pyroDown) are the seat's drafts. AMENDED 09-30b (his answers): phase 2 halves that fight's XP at its end (the party's own XP untouched: js/battle.js xpHalf); leaving the fight is a grid fight's thing only -- the 8-bit RUN takes him along, no harm, no foul; his fall's screen is his own line and a click to load; the road weighs him as 1.5.
entries.why: RULED 09-30, Griz: 'use a single attack with his regular mace in his main hand and then end turn, start using the mace of disruption and two attacks if he gets to half hp or a party member goes down ... If any character in the party leaves the fight, he goes into full lvl 12 combat until the fight is over, and player has to load from a save. If he ever goes down player has to load from a save.' 09-30b: 'every fight he guests with the party ... the party either loses half XP and continues, or it goes so bad they have to reload', 'he flips the mace of disruption to main hand if a party character has exited the fight'. The halving of each hero's XP (not the fight's) and the 8-bit RUN as leaving are the seat's readings, flagged for his word. Griz, 09-30b: "end of fight rewards /2 if pyro gets the disruptor out", "1 - that fight's xp", "2 - only the grid fights, no harm/foul on strategic withdrawals from random encounters", "3 - do 1.5, he'll likely tank a lot in that plate", "'the dwarf king fell in battle... well, obviously that didn't happen. (click to load)".

entries.what: The Ledger-Lamp in both games' fights and the field: the hooded lantern's law at bright 40 ft and dim 40 more (hood down: dim 5 ft), never spent, one hand, offered at the camp's A LIGHT IN HAND when the pack has it; it keeps its highway light, the seals and the roper's check (possession, lit or in the pack).
entries.why: RULED 09-30, Griz: 'now should function like a lantern but better' -- '3 perfect' (the seat's proposal, handoff-2026-09-30-the-settling-and-pyro.md §2C). Built by a runner 09-30b.

entries.what: The wet's grid keeps the party till one of them walks off it (the south edge, or up the stair): nothing dead, asleep, fed or quiet ends it now; all of them down is still lost, and a hero down still brings the herd. Out with something dead behind them: a win, its XP at the 8-bit's Victory; else a run. They come up in the 8-bit on the square he walked off at (up the stair: into warrens_b as the stair takes them). The landlord fed from the bucket pays 500 XP, shared among those standing like a fight's, once, on the grid or at the rim (LOWER THE BUCKET): 'The landlord is fed, and lets the wet be. 500 XP for the bucket: each fighter standing gains {n} XP.' (text.json w.fedXp; js/events.js EV.wetOut, EV.fedXp; deep16/js/wet.js). A walk-out plays no game-over tune. 09-30e: the bucket pays 125% of the otyugh's XP (1800 -> 2250), shared among those standing (w.fedXp: 'The landlord is fed, and lets the wet be. Each fighter standing gains {n} XP.'). Stepping onto the south line or the stair asks LEAVE THE AREA? YES / NO ('Up the stair' / 'Out of the wet to the south': all of you go with <name>; a foe in reach gets its swing); NO stands there, LEAVE THE FIGHT still on the ring; an AI-run hero is not asked. No card on the way out (the leave card and the ending's head both gone). They land on the 8-bit square the one who walked off left by before the 8-bit ending runs; by the stair: on the stair, the Victory and the bucket's XP, then up.
entries.why: RULED 09-30d, Griz: 'Can we keep on the grid after everything is dead (or as yet unrevealed) (assuming only exit is to the south) and do have the xp award when the players finally leave it (500 xp if we aren't giving any for bucket the landlord)'. The seat's calls, his to overrule: the 500 shared among those standing (not 500 each); the stair counts as a way out beside the south edge; the landing square; the line's words; a save already fed pays at the next trip or at the rim. RULED 09-30e, Griz: '1 - let's make it 125% the xp they get if they kill it' -- '2 - stair exit is good. Do an auto-pop-up 'leave the area? yes/no' when they hit the stairs or the south line - there's a popup from after the card we removed or something - the wet, out the way they came in - let's remove that.' -- 'the exit square on return to 8-bit should match where the character that triggers the exit, exits. True for stair exit as well, though I think you'll have to land them on the stair, reward and then stair them up.' The prompt's words are the seat's.

entries.what: A lantern or the Ledger-Lamp, once lit, stays in the hand: map to map, through a rest, out of a fight on lit ground, both games and the seam. A torch still goes out at a rest or leaving the map. The field's EQUIP has a LIGHT row while a hero holds one (grey in a fight's EQUIP): (put it away) -- the lantern or the lamp back in the pack -- or, for a torch, (put it out), spent (js/scenes.js equipHero; js/events.js EV.torchOut(all)). 09-30e: a rest puts any light away (a lantern or the lamp back in the pack); only a map change leaves a lantern lit.
entries.why: RULED 09-30d, Griz: 'I don't mind torches working that way, but using a lantern should stick using. I equipped in silverton was off by first random in the warrens. Equipped in the warrens, didn't carry over as in Aurdin's hand when the Wet triggered.' The seat's calls: through a rest too; the EQUIP LIGHT row (a light that sticks needs a way out of the hand). RULED 09-30e, Griz: '3 - let the rest put the light away'.

entries.what: When the herd comes in (deep16/js/wet.js W.noticed): their Stealth, rolled once and never shown (d20 + the crawler's DEX, +1), against each standing hero's passive Perception. Noticed: the camera on the first crawler, held 75 frames, 'Your comrade's fall has attracted the herd.' Unnoticed: nothing said, they walk in out of the dark. The landlord's watching card: the camera on it, held 60 frames (was 12). The clackers' picture: a chip-synth chitin click ('clack', js/audio.js) each time a claw snaps shut, ten in its 150 frames. The edge's prompt line: '<name> goes, and the party goes too.'

entries.what: The Wet, 09-30g. The landlord's rim (the 8-bit's picture squares, (7-10, 8)) takes the party onto the grid on the square stepped on, the landlord asleep in its water and its bucket picture before anyone moves; fed or dead, the rim is only stone. Fed, the landlord sinks on its next turn ('The landlord settles, fed, and sinks out of sight under the fall.'), off the grid and out of the order, whoever stands at its edge, and it is never on the grid again. The bucket is one hero's: whoever took it up (the lead at the station, or whoever walks onto it on the grid); the others' ITEM greys it ('<name> carries it'); the carrier down, it rolls onto the nearest free ground for another to walk onto. A bound landlord with nobody in reach churns where it can be seen (the camera on it, its flinch, 60 frames). The herd comes in at full speed again. 09-30g (later): awake with no one standing it could get at this turn (keeping to its water), the landlord sinks and waits ('The landlord sinks under the fall, and waits.'): off the grid, out of the order at the next turn's start, its wounds kept, not killed; a hero who ends a move where it could reach rises it ('(it was waiting)'). entries.what: Hideous Laughter's hyena, 09-30h (DEEP16). I'm assuming clackers will plot at least some of the deepholm expansion.'

entries.what: DEEP16: the roper's Reel (after its four tendril attacks, before the bite) pulls each creature it holds up to 25 ft a square at a time along the line to its nearest square -- the straight step, else a side step that still closes -- through the dragged one's friends' squares but not its foes', landing on the last square on the way it can stand in; where the line ends on a taken square beside the roper (a friend down there), the open square beside it nearest, if the 25 ft reaches it (js/ai.js reel).
entries.why: RULED 10-01e, Griz: 'yes, we've often been too lenient, 4 please' (the SRD's four tendrils and Reel, for two tendrils that each dragged its one all the way in). The SRD says 'straight toward it' and names no square where the way is blocked; passing through friends is the SRD's movement rule; the fallback square is the seat's call, after the bench's fights stalled on a fallen friend in the line.

entries.what: The roper's tendril is struck at from wherever the one it holds could be struck from: beside that one with a blade, or a shot at its square (DEEP16, 10-02: js/battle.js tendrilOn, strikeTendril). The weapon's own dice; no Sneak Attack, smite or mark on it, those being for a creature. A natural 1 lands on the one it holds, as at a darkmantle on a friend's head.
entries.why: SRD 5.1 says each tendril can be attacked (AC 20, 10 HP) and names no square for it; the tendril runs from the roper to the one it holds, and the game needs one place to click. A tendril holding no one is coiled about its foot and cannot be struck (the seat's call).

entries.what: A roper's tendril cut or broken comes back one a turn, as its action, when it has no one held and no one in reach of what it has left (js/ai.js brute, 10-02). Till then it is one tendril short, and with none to throw its reach is the bite's and it walks in. AMENDED 10-02 on his word ("1 - SRD is free but then never walks, correct?" / "go with SRD for combat"): every tendril cut or broken is back at its next turn, free (js/rules.js startTurn); the extruding as its action is gone. It walks in only when nothing it has can hold anyone: none to throw, every tendril holding, or no one in its reach it can hold (Freedom of Movement; js/ai.js usableOn, reachOf).
entries.why: SRD 5.1: 'Destroying a tendril deals no damage to the roper, which can extrude a replacement tendril on its next turn' -- one, and the seat reads the extruding as what the turn does. Griz's test, 10-02: 'have the party keep their distance and kill all the tendrils, then see if it walks to bite' -- with all of them back at once, or one back free at the start of every turn, it never would. RULED: the SRD for combat. A tendril holding no one is not struck and not targeted (RULED 10-02: "perfect, i assume also not targeted").

entries.what: DEEP16's Ready action has one trigger: the first foe that comes within reach of the readied weapon, or into sight and range for a bow, a thrown weapon or a readied attack spell (js/battle.js exec 'ready', readyHook, 10-02). The readied action is a single weapon attack, or an attack-shaped spell (an attack roll, rays, darts) cast now and held under concentration, its slot spent; a readied move is not built. 10-02 later, SUPERSEDED in part on Griz's word ("what if we use the menu you used to give 2 or 3 trigger conditions, then they navigate the wheel to what they're readying - yes closer to SRD"; "go with 1&2 - let's make 3 'an ally goes down' for readied healers. foe casts a spell you can see, if you mean foe you can see casts a spell"; "or were you letting them pick target when the trigger went off, that's probably better"): four triggers now -- a foe within reach (into sight for a bow or a spell), a foe's attack at one of us in sight (you too), one of us down (heard: no sight asked), a foe in sight casting a spell (told after it finishes: not Counterspell) -- picked from a numbered menu, then the wheel holds only what can be readied (the weapon or the other one, any spell that takes an action, by level, the tiers greyed where there is no slot, or a move up to the speed). Sprung, a player's hero aims it then (js/ui.js req.aim: the cursor on the one that set it off, X or the right button holds it and the ready waits); the AI's goes where the trigger points (battle.js readyAuto). 10-05: trigger 1 for a bow or a spell springs when a foe comes into sight OR one already in sight moves (a climb up a face, a step part way up a rope too); a hand that holds is not asked again for the same foe's same move, and the readied action stays for the next trigger till the start of the readier's turn.
entries.why: SRD 5.1's Ready takes any perceivable circumstance and any action; the grid can ask one question and answer it from what it sees -- a burrower up out of the ground, a phase spider out of the Ethereal, one walking up, the invisible seen. The handoff of 10-01e asked for this one ('when a foe comes up in my reach'). The seat's calls inside his: 'one of us' counts the readier; 'one of us goes down' is told after the blow, the spell or the turn that did it; a readied self-spell asks CAST or HOLD instead of an aim; the AI still readies only against what is under the ground or out of the world, on the first trigger. Griz, 10-05: "just OR if there's already in sight - there's times when players ready to let an ally go first - is it such that a refused 'trigger' waits for the next fire?" (Aurdin's readied Scorching Ray let the male giant climb in plain view twice). Asked once a move is the seat's.

entries.what: The bulette bites and goes under again in the same turn when it has 5 ft of its move left, leaving the reach of those beside it as any creature does -- their opportunity attacks first -- and digs on as far from them as the rest of its move goes (js/ai.js diveAfter, 10-02). The xorn stays up and fights. RULED 10-02 (Griz: "keep that, it's what people used to one will want anyway"): it dives after any blow it swung, hit or miss, never after a turn it struck at no one (js/ai.js diveAfter, turn.attacked).
entries.why: Griz, 10-01d: 'If the mechanics allow it and a smart player or AI would do it, we'll allow it.' The seat's call of 10-01d kept it up through the party's turns because nothing could answer it; Ready answers it now. The xorn, which resists plain steel and claws three times, has no cause to run (the seat's call).

entries.what: Aurdin's joke, 10-02 (DEEP16; the easter egg in place of #hyena-laughter-egg). Only in a fight the 8-bit game opened, only with a gnoll standing (a glory-seeker counts: the Snoot's young blood), only when Ink for Katarina is done (flag katVision: the sheet given), Hideous Laughter is in Aurdin's book and among the day's spells he brought: his own square is a target of it too (grimoire.js M.jokeReady, magic.js selfToo). Cast on himself: he goes down laughing (prone, incapacitated; the slot spent; what he concentrated on lets go); every hyena that hears it (any side; not one asleep, held, stunned or in the Ethereal) laughs till the end of its next turn, and every gnoll for two full rounds, from his turn to his turn two rounds on (M.jokeClock), with no save, not even when hurt; their reactions spent. Then his own fit passes (he stays prone), and the fight holds for the egg: a red pixel egg in the palette's reds, dithered, a white shine and a sweeping glint, sparks, popping in and bobbing, the line 'Guess I'm the Joke, Now' under it at twice size, about four seconds (E or a click after one goes on: the cutscene beat's own rule). Sounds: guffaw (his), gnollaugh (theirs), cackle (the hyenas), rimshot as the egg comes up, shine. The seat's calls: the glory-seeker as a gnoll; any side; who hears; the clock; prone after; the cards' lines ('Aurdin cracks up at his own joke, and goes down laughing.', 'The gnolls know that laugh. They go down howling with it'), the sounds and the egg's look are drafts. 10-02b: the gnolls' fit on their sheet's own LAUGH row, cut from Griz's gnoll sheet 2 (deep16/_src/gnoll_grok_2.webp, tools/gnoll-sheet.py): the yawn, sit/rest 2, 1, 3, 8, 3, fall/get-up 1, 2, 4, 2, then fall 5 / sit 8 / fall 5 / sit 8 over and over while it laughs (one already on the ground starts there); the laugh fires on the yawn, the fall's 4 and the first 8 of each chain (grimoire.js M.LAUGH, M.laughTick), one gnoll's at a time, so a pack laughs as one: at 0, 2.0 s and 3.0 s, then every 1.6 s; held still under the egg. Their PRONE row: Fall / Get Up 8, 7, 6, 5 (S.proneRow plays it forward to go down and back to get up). The seat's calls: each beat's hold, the quiet between laughs (the sound's own 0.83 s and a hair), a pack staggered by its place in the line-up, the fit held under the egg, the prone row's four frames. 10-02c: a cutscene first, as the darkness's: Aurdin waist up, shaking with it ('AURDIN CRACKS UP AT HIS OWN JOKE.', his guffaw); the camera tilting down to him on the floor ('AND GOES DOWN LAUGHING.', a little 'hehehe' once); the hyena's still face (his hehehe again); a gnoll's face pushed in on, then its yawn with its laugh ('THE GNOLLS KNOW THAT LAUGH.'), the camera pulling back to the fight -- then the effects as before. He picks himself up as that turn ends ('Aurdin picks himself up off the floor, still wheezing.'). Once the egg has come up, never again in that save (flag eggJoke). The gnolls' chain laughs on every other chain. Their prone: fall/get-up 1, 2 (over onto the back), and up by the sheet's own 3 to 8 (a `getup` row). The seat's calls: the captions, the hehehe, the framings and beat lengths.
entries.why: RULED 10-02, Griz: 'If and only if Gnolls are present in 16bit fight (main game only), and aurdin has done the silent quest and received and learned and selected it for the fight - he can cast hideous laughter on himself, in which case he goes into hideous laughter. As a reaction, any hyenas go into hideous laughter until the end of their next turn (not end of reaction) and any gnolls go into hideous laughter for 2 full rounds without save. after their reactions have played, hideous laughter on aurdin expires - battle pauses and big red shiny easter egg on screen: "Guess I'm the Joke, Now" for a few seconds then resume' (the silent quest read as the unjournaled one, EV.UNJOURNALED) 10-02b, Griz: 'assuming their standing I'd play 'yawn' (idle variation 6) when the laugh sound fires, then like sit/rest 2, 1, 3, 8 .. 3 to fall/getup 1, 2, 4, 2,  - 5, sit/rest 8, fall/getup 5, sit/rest 8'; 'the 4 in 1, 2, 4, 2 is great, and on the first 8 in the 5sit/8rest/5sit/8rest chain'. 10-02c, Griz: 'Aurdin gets to get up after he ends the turn he cast the spell, and him being able to cast it on himself again should be disabled when the egg appears (1 per customer)'; 'Like those cut scenes, with Aurdin waist up and laugh, the cam down to him down with the laugh and a give him a little hehehe that plays once showing him - then zoom on idol face living gnoll, then idle 6 with the sound (with the text overlaying as appropriate) then zoomed back out and the effects we currently have start'; 'oh, hehehe from aurdin again on the still face of the hyena'; '1 every other chain'; '2 yes'.

entries.what: DEEP16's Counterspell (10-02, Griz: "Yeah, that's an important one to have in there"): asked as a spell is released (js/magic.js M.cast, js/grimoire.js M.counterAsk) of each foe of the caster who knows it, has a 3rd-or-higher slot and its reaction, and sees the caster within 60 ft; a player's hero picks the slot or lets it go, the AI counters any levelled spell but a friend's blessing on a friend, with the lowest slot that makes it fail outright, else its highest. Not asked: a readied spell's release, a spell used again, a cantrip by the AI; a Counterspell is not itself countered. On the generic wizard's, sorcerer's and warlock's 3rd-level lists (js/classes.js), last. Dispel Magic takes an empty square in the area of a spell (Griz: "I like 'spell effect squares without people' as valid dispel targets for that spell"): the spell the Globe's stamp says laid it (castId) ends by Dispel's own rule; two on one square, the player's caster is asked which.
entries.why: SRD 5.1's Counterspell and Dispel Magic ("Choose one creature, object, or magical effect within range"); the AI's choice, the order in the lists and the which-of-two prompt are the seat's. A creature's own power is no spell (RULED 10-02, Griz: "no to creature abilities"): the darkmantle's aura has no castId and is not a target.

entries.what: The seat's and the runners' calls inside the SRD pass of 10-02 (Griz: "SRD as we can, yes - with noted exceptions"; "yes to 1-7 and the smaller ones"): Dispel Magic on a creature ends whole (for all a spell holds) Banishment, Haste, Polymorph, Enlarge/Reduce, Animal Shapes, Mislead, Etherealness, Gaseous Form and the Dominates, whose ending does more than lift what is on the one; a readied Dash is the MOVE (a reaction's move up to the speed), so DASH is not on the Ready wheel; the bulette's leap pushes no one (it lands beside its mark, so no one is in its space); the spy's Cunning Action is the goblin's Nimble Escape for now (Disengage and a step back; Dash and Hide not read); Sleep's minute runs on its caster's turns; a bound monster weighs its attacks from the squares it can stand on.
entries.why: Where the SRD leaves the grid a choice, or the grid cannot yet do the whole of a rule: the exceptions are named so they can be found and finished.

entries.what: The Pocket DM's ladder (10-02): four rungs from the dial's table, each about a third again the last in CR on a map drawn fresh; SHORT REST FOR THE WICKED between -- the fallen up at 1 HP first ("SRD + free rez for the fallen before the short rest applies is good"), then hit dice till whole or out (one a level a run), the short-rest features and a warlock's slots back, a wizard's Arcane Recovery once a run; LONG REST FOR THE TRIAL after the fourth win, then the trial, double deadly (the smallest table whose adjusted XP is twice the party's deadly threshold), which unlocks Pyro on the roster ("give them a 'long rest for the trial' after the fourth win and then do your double deadly"). A loss: quit, retry or reroll the rung, the party as it went in ("restored to what they went in with before they died"). The fights kept with notes, saved as a file, mailed, or carried to his Discord ("also put my discord link"). entries.what: The Keeper of the Flooded Stair, ours and not the SRD's Water Weird: above the water a Slam (DC 15 STR or prone) and, each round as a bonus action, the Wave up the stair (STR DC 13 or prone) that bounces off the front wall and sweeps the prone 10 ft toward the deep, where they stand up free; one washed onto a deep square is restrained and the Keeper pours into the water around it (AC 10; its bonus action there, Active Suffocation); drowning is 1d6 less CON (at least 1) at the start of the victim's turn, twice after an Active Suffocation, and a blow to the Keeper in the water is a CON concentration check (DC 10 or half) whose failure frees the victim of the hold but not of the drowning; the Ice Wall, 3 uses, readied and sprung by a hero moving toward the exit (the SRD's Wall of Ice body: AC 12, 30 HP a 10-ft section) and a fire spell destroys a section at once; a cold area spell freezes the water (1d4 cold to the caster's friends in it, ice anchors against the backwash and is not the deep). Not the SRD's: all of it but the wall's body and the concentration DC. 100 HP on the bench's word (the four kill 58 in 3 rounds).
entries.why: Griz 10-02/10-03 (handoff-2026-10-02-the-keeper.md; his answers: 'DC 15 STR save - using himself is more forceful than the wave', 'the roll twice, each floored at 1', row 11, 'ready the wall with a trigger of party member moves toward exit', '10 ft per wave', 'any water square next to the victim')

entries.what: The Spy's Cunning Action (SRD 5.1: a bonus action to Dash, Disengage or Hide) is chosen by the grid so: pressed (hurt under half with a foe beside it, or two beside it under three quarters) it Disengages, steps to the square farthest from the party with a clear crossbow line and no one beside it, and shoots; with no one in reach by the walk but one in reach by walk and Dash it Dashes to close; running for the stair it Dashes again, or Disengages first if a hero beside it still has a reaction; it Hides after its turn only where no foe sees it clearly (the same seenBy question as the Hide action). Stealth +6 on its sheet.
entries.why: The SRD gives the Spy the bonus action and no policy; the class NPC rogue's choices (js/features.js, js/tactics.js) copied for a stat block. Thresholds are the seat's (10-02 cloud seat).

entries.what: A foe with two ranged weapons and no ranged Multiattack (the gnoll's longbow and thrown spear) uses the likelier, bigger blow at the lowest AC it sees, a thrown weapon past its normal range at disadvantage: the spear within 20 ft, the bow beyond. `rangedMulti` on a sheet is its ranged Multiattack (the Bandit Captain's two thrown daggers); the melee `multi` stays the melee routine.
entries.why: SRD 5.1 gives the gnoll Spear (melee or 20/60) and Longbow, the Captain 'two ranged attacks with its daggers'; the grid's volley fired the first ranged attack once. Thrown weapons are not spent (as the javelins already are not).

entries.what: The Bandit Captain's Parry (+2 AC against one melee attack that would hit, a reaction, it must see the attacker and wield a melee weapon) is taken whenever the +2 turns the blow; never against a natural 20, a ranged attack or a spell that is not touch.
entries.why: SRD 5.1 Bandit Captain: Parry. The take-it-when-it-turns-the-blow policy is the same as the class NPC's Shield (js/battle.js attack).

entries.what: Duergar Resilience (advantage on saves against spells) holds for the saves a spell already running asks of a duergar (Spirit Guardians at its turn's start, a zone's, a web's, a wall's, the charm's on a hurt): while magic.js startTurn/endTurn and the stepInto/onHurt/confusedTurn/danceAsk chains resolve on it, B.spellRun names it. A concentration save is not against a spell.
entries.why: RU.save read B.castLevel only during the cast; SRD 5.1 says 'saving throws against ... spells'. A monster-born ground with no spell behind it, resolved in the same chains, would get it too (none exists on a duergar's turn now).

entries.what: The dragonborn and the tiefling on the grid: each class figure (npc<class>_p0) with the race laid over it, npc<class>_dragonborn_p0 and npc<class>_tiefling_p0, the class's kit, weapon and attack kept (tools/lpc-compose.py RACE_LOOKS). The dragonborn is gold (LPC skin all.lpcr.amber: the gold dragon's, fire, a 15-ft cone), with the lizard head of the class figure's sex, no hair, the dragon ears and a lizard tail, and no wings. The tiefling is garnet-skinned (all.lpcr.garnet) and keeps the class's human head and hair (the druid takes the human female head for Higertha's orc one); curled bone-yellow horns are drawn over a hood or a hat, and a lizard tail matches the skin. The Pocket DM and the camp draw a made character of either race with these (deep16/js/classes.js classLook); every other race keeps the class figure.
